conditions.overall: Low and clear across most Watauga and Ashe County streams. Stocking reduced due to Setzer Hatchery renovation — check ncpaws.org before planning around fresh stockings.

top_flies.name: Sulphur Dry
top_flies.note: Evening hatch kicking in on the Watauga DH and South Fork. Late afternoon into dusk.

top_flies.name: Sparkle Dun (Sulphur)
top_flies.note: Fish in the film before the duns are fully out. Very effective right now.

top_flies.name: Yellow Sally
top_flies.note: DSO calls this the yellow bug transition. Dry dropper with yellow Stimulator as the dry.

top_flies.name: Elk Hair Caddis (Tan)
top_flies.note: Still producing on wild water. Transitioning out of peak caddis season.

top_flies.name: Frenchie
top_flies.note: Subsurface go-to on pressured DH water. Dead-drift near bottom.

tactics: Low clear water — use 5–6X tippet across all water types
Dry dropper rig over any large indicator in current conditions
Size down your dry fly — fish are seeing everything right now
Best fishing on wild stretches, not DH, for natural hatches
Evening is the prime window — Sulphurs and Yellow Sallies late afternoon through dusk

waters.name: Watauga River (Valle Crucis DH)
waters.note: Artificials only, catch-and-release until June 5. Evening Sulphur hatch producing. Harvest opens June 6 — verify at ncwrc.gov.

waters.name: South Fork New River
waters.note: Low and clear. Wild stretches fishing better than stocked sections right now. Caddis and early Sulphurs.

waters.name: Meat Camp Creek
waters.note: Hatchery supported. Go early on stocking week — pressure builds fast. Caddis and nymphs.

elevation_note: High Country streams (Boone area, 3,300–4,000 ft) run 1–2 weeks behind lower-elevation WNC. Sulphur timing here is late May into June.
stocking_note: Setzer State Fish Hatchery under renovation through 2028. Stocking reduced and unpredictable. April 2026 saw no DH stocking at all. Check ncpaws.org daily before planning around fresh fish.
